# cb:b135

> Contracts govern behavior across fundamentally different substrates. A single state-machine contract was independently implemented in compiled code and in agent reasoning, producing identical results without either knowing about the other. The contract served as intermediary: a domain expert authors it, an architect verifies against it, implementations derive from it.

**Type:** attestation · **Kind:** design-observation · **Domain:**  · **Status:** active
**Created:** 2026-03-23

**Artifact:** [`document:design-notes`](../../../design-notes)

## Evidence

1. **2026-03-23** - Two implementations were tested against the same record: both rejected an invalid transition when required fields were missing, both accepted a valid one. Neither knew about the other. The contract governed behavior across two fundamentally different substrates - compiled code and agent reasoning - without modification.
